claim: A general, population-level post-hoc calibration model (Platt scaling) applied to code LLM confidence does not, on average, improve the alignment between model confidence and real developer acceptance behavior at scale.
stance_target: the calibration disconnect finding (expressed confidence fails to communicate real uncertainty even after post-hoc correction)
scope_conditions: 24 million real-world developer interactions across multiple programming languages, in-IDE code completion context
quoted_support: We find that a general, post-hoc calibration model based on Platt-scaling does not, on average, improve the reliability of model confidence signals.

claim: Dynamically personalizing confidence calibration to individual developers can be effective, but effectiveness depends heavily on the volume of that user's interaction data (a cold-start limitation).
stance_target: feasibility of personalized calibration as a fix for the expressed-interface disconnect
scope_conditions: per-user calibration within the same 24M-interaction in-IDE dataset
quoted_support: We also find that while dynamically personalizing calibration to individual users can be effective, its effectiveness is highly dependent on the volume of user interaction data.

claim: Professional developers and expert designers prefer non-numerical, color-coded reliability indicators over numeric confidence scores for in-editor code generation.
stance_target: human-facing confidence communication should be coarse/categorical rather than precise/numeric
scope_conditions: multi-phase design study: 3 expert designers, 153 professional developers; scenario-based design, semi-structured interviews, survey validation
quoted_support: revealing a clear preference for presenting reliability signals via non-numerical, color-coded indicators within the in-editor code generation workflow.

claim: This study builds a scalable, flexible calibration framework that can obtain calibration weights for open-source code models using any dataset, but evaluates only single-pass/token-level model confidence, not repeated-sampling (self-consistency) confidence.
stance_target: gap: sampling-based confidence untested as the underlying signal for in-IDE calibration at scale
quoted_support: we develop a scalable and flexible calibration framework which can be used to obtain calibration weights for open-source models using any dataset, and evaluate whether calibrators improve the alignment between model confidence and developer acceptance behavior.

claim: Developer acceptance behavior, rather than functional correctness, is used as the ground-truth acceptability measure that calibration is evaluated against, which is a distinct downstream utility metric from pass@1/AUROC-vs-correctness used in most calibration papers.
stance_target: downstream utility metric choice for calibration evaluation
scope_conditions: in-IDE code completion, real developer interaction logs
quoted_support: Post-hoc calibration of internal model confidences aims to align probabilities with an acceptability measure.
